hypothesis: The 5 elaboration errors are NOT the top/reorder_buffer port mismatch that attempt 1 fixed (that was already corrected and the same category of failure persists). The surviving blocker is a multiple-driver / net-elaboration problem created by the `sorry: constant selects in always_* processes` pattern: several modules assign a constant bit- or part-select on the LHS of an `always_comb`/`always_ff` (e.g. a `valid`/`ready`/epoch field or an array word written as `reg[i] <= ...` with a literal index), while the same vector is also assigned elsewhere (a separate reset `always_ff`, a second `always_comb`, or a continuous assign). Icarus collapses the constant select to 'all bits included', which makes the whole vector appear driven from two processes; that surfaces as unresolved-net/multiple-driver and 'output port expression must support continuous assignment' elaboration failures. The offending sites are around generated_attempt2.sv:284 (a cache/predictor state/output vector) and :954 (a top-level/control vector), i.e. dcache.sv, branch_predictor.sv, and the residual double-driven nets in rv32i5.sv (dc_idle / squash_valid / busy-valid style nets that attempt 1 declared but did not fully single-drive).
